      Equaliser

      A story in eight sounds

      Bitty listens to Earth

      Bitty is a space pup with very good ears. Satellites send Bitty Earth’s numbers, and Bit2Beat turns them into music. Follow eight short chapters of real NASA and USGS data, from a warming century to the planet’s breath. Each chapter plays in the studio’s own player, so you can open any of them and keep exploring.

        Epilogue

        Your turn

        About Bit2Beat

        Bit2Beat is our entry to the NASA Space Apps Challenge “Earth Information Jukebox”. It turns Earth data into sound, so anyone, including people who are blind or have low vision, can follow how our planet changes by listening.

        How it works

        Every number becomes a note: higher values play higher. Each series is scaled between its own lowest and highest value (or a range shared with series in the same unit) and placed on a musical scale, so equal steps in the data sound like equal steps in the melody. Position in time can also become position in space, from simple stereo to 7.1.4 surround.

        The data comes from NASA GISTEMP, NASA POWER and NASA EONET, the NASA Earth Information Center (Scientific Visualization Studio) and the USGS earthquake feed. When there is no internet, Bit2Beat uses real copies of those feeds saved inside the app. Everything runs in your browser; your files never leave your computer.

        Our vision

        We as a team enjoyed making this from scratch. We experienced and learned a lot during the time, and we had to know each other well. Every one of us contributed and gave all he had.

        Our vision is to help first: free technology like this can open data to people who cannot see a chart, and anyone who tries it for fun learns something about Earth along the way.

        Data sources & credits

        • NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4) — data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp
        • NASA POWER daily and monthly point data — power.larc.nasa.gov
        • NASA Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker (EONET v3) — eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov
        • NASA GIBS satellite imagery (MODIS, VIIRS) — gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov
        • NASA Image and Video Library (Bitty’s notes) — images.nasa.gov
        • USGS Earthquake Hazards Program real-time feeds — earthquake.usgs.gov
        • abcjs music engraving (MIT licence)

        Use Bit2Beat by speaking, in English or your own language: say “play”, “pause”, “next”, “search for sea ice” or “help”. Press Enter for yes, Escape for no. You can always press V.

        Accessibility

        Saved on this device.

        How to use Bit2Beat

        1. Find something to hear. Search NASA’s Earth Information Center above the tabs (turn on AI mode to ask in your own words), or pick from the menu. Image turns a map or picture into sound, Video follows a NASA animation or time-lapse, Earth events plays natural events and earthquakes across the map, Data plays climate series and your own CSV.
        2. Press Play. Higher values play higher. The Melody panel and the score show the same notes.
        3. Shape the sound. Pick a mood (sad, happy or excited), change instrument, scale and tempo, mute or solo channels, or press Smart Tuning.
        4. Export. Download audio, the notes as CSV or the score.

        Keyboard

        Space
        Play / pause
        ← →
        Step back / forward and hear that step
        Home End
        First / last step
        L
        Repeat on / off
        D
        Read the data summary aloud (press again to pause, and again to carry on)
        G
        Bitty’s guide
        Esc
        Stop reading aloud, close the guide
        T
        Readings table
        + − 0
        Scientific maps: zoom in, zoom out, whole map (also the mouse wheel; drag to move)
        V
        Voice control on / off: say “play”, “pause”, “next”, “where am I”, “search for sea ice”, “go to video”, “violin”, “7.1”, “help” or “stop voice control”
